items.definition: Physical harm to a part of the body, usually caused by an accident or by playing sport.
examples: He missed the whole season because of a knee injury.

items.definition: To hurt a joint, such as your ankle or wrist, by twisting it suddenly.
examples: I sprained my ankle when I missed the last step.

items.definition: A piece of paper or an electronic record from a doctor that allows you to get a particular medicine.
examples: The doctor gave me a prescription for antibiotics.
You can only buy this cream with a prescription.

trap.en: A recipe is instructions for cooking. A doctor's note for medicine is a prescription.
trap.es: La «receta del médico» es a prescription. Recipe solo se usa para cocinar.

items.definition: Unable to empty your bowels easily.
examples: Eating more fibre helps if you often feel constipated.

trap.en: Constipated has nothing to do with a cold. If you have a cold, say I've got a cold or I've got a blocked nose.
trap.es: «Estoy constipado» (resfriado) NO es I'm constipated, que significa «estreñido». Di I've got a cold.

items.definition: To do physical exercise in order to keep fit or build muscle.
examples: I work out at the gym three times a week.
She works out every morning before breakfast.

items.definition: A routine medical or dental examination to see whether you are healthy.
examples: I'm due for a dental check-up next month.

items.definition: An unwanted effect of a medicine, in addition to the way it is meant to help you.
examples: The tablets can cause side effects such as headaches and drowsiness.

items.definition: Having a bad physical reaction, such as a rash or sneezing, to a certain food, substance or animal.
examples: My brother is allergic to nuts, so he always checks the labels.

items.definition: To eat, drink or do less of something, usually because it is bad for you.
examples: My doctor told me to cut down on salt and fried food.
I'm trying to cut down on coffee.

items.definition: To start to suffer from an illness, usually a mild one.
examples: Half the office has come down with the flu this week.

items.definition: Painful and uncomfortable, especially after exercise or because of an infection.
examples: My legs are sore after yesterday's run.
I woke up with a sore throat.

items.definition: The physical or mental strength that lets you keep doing something difficult for a long time.
examples: Marathon runners need great stamina as well as good technique.

items.definition: The part of a hospital in Britain that treats people who need urgent help, for example after an accident. Its full name is accident and emergency.
examples: We spent four hours in A&E after he fell off his bike.

items.definition: A shop where you can buy medicine, toiletries and other health products. In Britain it is also called a pharmacy.
examples: I'll pop into the chemist's to pick up some cough syrup.
collocations: the chemist's on the high street

items.definition: Affected by alcohol or drugs so that you cannot think or behave normally.
examples: The driver was clearly intoxicated and was arrested at the scene.

trap.en: Intoxicated means drunk or under the influence of drugs. If bad food made you ill, you have food poisoning.
trap.es: «Me intoxiqué con el marisco» se dice I got food poisoning. Intoxicated significa «ebrio» o «bajo los efectos de drogas».
